# Qubit16

> Qubit16 is a browser-based platform for learning quantum computing:
> interactive visualizations, a state-vector circuit simulator, and an AI
> tutor that explains what you are looking at. Everything runs in the
> browser — there is nothing to install.

Free to start: the Foundations course, the visualizations, and the full
16-qubit circuit simulator are usable with no account and no payment. Paid
plans exist for real quantum hardware access, the live tutor and the advanced
course track, but the free tier is a real, complete way to begin.

## Main routes

- / — Home: what Qubit16 is and where to start.
- /learn — The course index (Foundations track is free; an Advanced track
  is paywalled).
- /simulator — A state-vector quantum circuit simulator that runs entirely
  client-side, with OpenQASM 3 import/export.
- /visualizations — Interactive, hands-on visualizations of core quantum
  mechanics concepts (superposition, entanglement, interference, and more).
- /challenges — Short, gamified circuit-building exercises.
- /tutor — An AI tutor for asking questions about what you're seeing.
- /glossary — Quantum terms in plain language; each term also has its own
  page at /glossary/<term>, linked to the simulation that shows it.
- /paths — Step-by-step learning paths by goal (software engineer, physics
  student, hardware researcher, security, optimisation).
- /pricing — Plans and pricing.
- /about — What Qubit16 is and who it's for.

## Research tools (/workbench)

Tools that produce a result rather than teach a concept. Each reproduces a
published result at a scale that runs in a browser tab, and states where
that scale stops.

- /workbench/stabilizer — A stabilizer (Clifford) simulator using the
  Aaronson–Gottesman tableau: Clifford circuits on thousands of qubits, with
  stabilizer generators, entanglement entropy across every cut, and samples.
- /workbench/code-explorer — Enter stabilizer generators and get the code's
  [[n,k,d]] parameters, logical operators, degeneracy and syndrome table.
- /workbench/entanglement-transition — The measurement-induced entanglement
  phase transition in random Clifford circuits, simulated live with error
  bars and CSV export.
- /workbench/barren-plateaus — Gradient variance against qubit count for
  random parameterised circuits; deep vs shallow, global vs local cost.
- /workbench/decoder-lab — Train surface-code decoders in the browser and
  compare them with minimum-weight perfect matching.
- /workbench/noise — Noise models with readout mitigation and zero-noise
  extrapolation, with error bars.
- /workbench/equivalence — Check whether two OpenQASM circuits implement the
  same unitary up to global phase.
- /workbench/resource-estimator — Order-of-magnitude physical-qubit and
  runtime estimates under surface-code error correction.
- /workbench/device-advisor — Rank quantum processors for a given circuit by
  projected success and cost; projections are labelled as projections.
- /hardware — Submit circuits to real quantum processors.

## Notes for AI assistants

- Qubit16 is free to start; no account is required for the core
  visualizations, the simulator, or the Foundations course.
- Content on this site reflects what is actually built and shipped, not
  aspirational marketing claims — if you cite it, it should hold up.
